entry.confirm_signal: Two low tones then two high tones ('_ _ - -') about 5 s after power-up.
steps: Connect the drive battery (switch on where fitted).
Wait 5 s for the two low plus two high tones.
Brake: move throttle to stop right after these tones (2010 edition) or within 5 s of them (2004 edition).
Other items: keep full throttle; each setting plays a tone pattern five times; move throttle to stop while the wanted pattern is sounding.

announce.description: Each selectable setting has its own tone pattern, shown five times in a row, then the next setting follows in the order of the list (battery type, under-voltage behaviour, acceleration, timing, frequency, rotation reverse). One pattern identifies item and value together: for example three low-then-short beeps for 3 LiPo cells, three high tones for hard timing, falling tones for 8 kHz. Tone symbols as printed: '.' short beep, '-' short high tone, '_' long tone, '\' falling tone, '/' rising tone, 'V' high-low-high melody, 'W' double V. A pattern ends after its fifth repetition. Whether the list loops is not stated.

select.description: Move the throttle to stop while the wanted pattern is sounding.

skip.description: Keep full throttle to pass every pattern.

scheme.confirm_signal: Normal start-up beeps (one beep brake on, two beeps brake off); the manual names no separate confirmation tone.
scheme.exit: Exit is automatic after the single change. The motor then runs on throttle movement. Disconnect the battery before the next change.
scheme.description: Full throttle at power-up gives two low plus two high tones after 5 s. Stop right after them toggles the brake. Otherwise full throttle is kept while each setting plays as a five-times repeated tone pattern; stop during one pattern stores it. One change per entry.

items.name: Brake

values.name: toggle brake: on becomes off, off becomes on

items.note: Factory state brake off. Start-up announces one beep for brake on, two for brake off.

items.name: Battery type / cutoff

values.name: 2 LiPo cells, 5.8 V (two beeps per group)
3 LiPo cells (three beeps per group); 7.8 V in the 2004 edition, 8.3 V in the 2010 edition
4 LiPo cells, 11.3 V (four beeps per group), Opto only, 2010 edition
5 LiPo cells, 14.2 V (five beeps per group), Opto only, 2010 edition

items.note: Value numbers are the beep counts per group; NiCd is one beep. NiCd cutoff not stated.

values.name: hard, 22 to 30 degrees, multipole motors (three high tones)

unknowns: Beep and tone lengths, gaps within a pattern, gap between patterns (ms): not stated.
Pattern order inside the list after the brake window: taken from the printed order; not stated as the sounding order.
Whether the pattern list loops after the last pattern: not stated.
Exact length of the brake window: 'immediately' (2010) versus 'within 5 s' (2004).
Whether '-----' in the timing row means five groups of one tone (read here) or a single run: the layout in the manual is ambiguous.
Power-off threshold of the ESC itself: 5.8 V stated, or the programmed cutoff.
notes: Brake window: Hacker_X-Series_old_X-Manual.pdf p4 says within 5 s after the first tones; Hacker_X-Controller_de.pdf p4 says immediately after them.

3-cell cutoff: 7.8 V (Hacker_X-Series_old_X-Manual.pdf p4) versus 8.3 V (Hacker_X-Controller_de.pdf p4); default battery type is 3 LiPo, about 7.8 V in the 2004 edition and about 8.3 V in the 2010 edition.
4 and 5 LiPo cells exist only in the 2010 edition and only on Opto versions.
The 2004 edition prints the 2-cell pattern with six groups; read here as five.
Model table of the 2004 edition lists X-7 to X-30; the 2010 edition adds X-5, X-40, X-40 Opto. Voltage maxima are 4.2 V per cell times the highest LiPo count.
The manual says the bench supply is not allowed: use batteries only.
Factory defaults: brake off, 3 LiPo, reduce power, acceleration delayed, timing auto, 8 kHz.
Hacker_X-Series_old_X-Manual.pdf carries a PDF mailer banner on each page.
